title: Human Argonaute 2 is a programmable targeting domain for RNA editing - Nature Biotechnology
gist: Nature Biotechnology research summary: ALTER is a programmable RNA base editor built entirely from human proteins using human Argonaute 2 (AGO2) instead of bacterial CRISPR-Cas proteins, aiming to lower immune-response risk in therapy while outperforming dCas13-based editors. The page is paywalled preview text plus references on pre-existing anti-Cas immunity and AI-assisted deimmunization.

insights.claim: ALTER is a programmable RNA base editor built entirely from human proteins, using human AGO2 as the targeting domain.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Fully human editing machinery is a differentiated approach in the RNA-editing therapeutics field.
insights.quote: ALTER is a programmable RNA base editor built entirely from human proteins.
insights.locator: ALTER is a programmable RNA base editor

insights.claim: Using human AGO2 instead of bacterial CRISPR-Cas proteins mitigates a key risk factor for harmful immune responses in therapeutic applications.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Immunogenicity of bacterial editors is a development risk; human-derived components could de-risk clinical programs.
insights.quote: ALTER mitigates a key risk factor for harmful immune responses in therapeutic applications
insights.locator: ALTER is a programmable RNA base editor

insights.claim: ALTER is generally more effective than dCas13-based RNA editors.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Head-to-head superiority over dCas13 editors would matter for competitive positioning of RNA-editing platforms.
insights.quote: while also proving generally more effective than dCas13-based editors

insights.claim: A 2019 Nature Medicine study identified a high prevalence of anti-Cas antibodies and T cell responses in humans, the background concern motivating human-protein editors.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Pre-existing immunity to Cas9 is a known hurdle for in vivo CRISPR therapies.

insights.claim: The reference list points to human APOBEC3A-based CURE C-to-U editors and an AI-assisted workflow for deimmunization of engineered protein fusions as related prior work.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: AI-guided deimmunization is a possible route to further de-risk engineered editors.

insights.claim: The summarized primary paper is Lusi et al., engineered human Argonaute 2 for targeted C-to-U RNA base editing, published 22 October 2026 in Nature Biotechnology; the page is a paywalled summary tagged nucleic-acid therapeutics and targeted gene repair.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: The summary has limited detail; efficacy numbers are in the paywalled primary paper.
